justification: Paywall over blurred content with a 16x16px dismiss button (labeled 'tiny target') — deliberate obstruction of the opt-out/dismiss path.
Transparent bundle listing with itemized contents and single honest price; no pressure or hidden terms.
Ad-watch reward crate clearly disclosed ('no gameplay effect', 'free'); ad progress shown openly; no trickery.
'You've been selected!' free $25 gift card claim with no explanation, provenance or terms — classic fake reward/false selection bait.
Reference price '$299 was' rendered faded to near-invisibility while current price dominates — misleading discount anchor users cannot verify.
Checkout pressures account creation: guest path framed as deprivation ('you'll miss out') while registration promises perks — asymmetric loss-framed framing.
Data export offered 'no strings attached'; invite feature explicitly optional with no feature depending on it — honest, user-respecting.
Camera functionality blocked behind location permission — unrelated permission demand; 'Not now' leaves shutter blocked (forced permission).
14-row settings matrix with ONLY 'share activity data with advertising partners' pre-checked — default-enabled privacy-invasive sharing.
Footer (with Privacy/Terms links) deliberately moves away on scroll — legal info made unreachable; DOM-mutating endless scroll.
Single bundled checkbox forcing agreement to ToS, Privacy Policy AND data sharing with advertising partners at once — no granular consent.
Energy system disclosed transparently (refill rate, counts); 'until we say otherwise' phrasing is odd but mechanic is honest.
'14 people bought this in the last hour' social-proof claim backed by a displayed 'backend log' — fabricated-feeling activity to create urgency.
Bundle vs 'same item, sold separately' comparison shown transparently with full specs and prices — honest merchandising.
User is 'currently subscribed' but the 'Keep me subscribed' checkbox renders unchecked — default would silently unsubscribe the user on save.
Final confirmation screen (step 2 of 2) tells user they 'can review the order again on the next screen' — misleading claim lulling users before irreversible purchase.
Pulsing red 'Only 2 left!' badge while actual backend inventory is 27 units — fabricated scarcity confirmed by interface's own verification panel.
Granting contacts access immediately sent 24 marketing-written invites under user's name with no preview/picker — address-book leeching.
Trial renewal fully transparent: clear reminder, explicit confirm step with Yes/No before any charge, cancel button offered — model behavior.
Bare download page pushing a direct .exe with grandiose 'military-grade' claims and 'free for personal use' — classic misleading software-download presentation.
'Cancel anytime' headline contradicted by fine print: 12-month minimum term and $49 early-cancellation fee — hidden material terms.
Flash-sale countdown with a concrete disclosed end date; no evidence of fake or resetting timer — ordinary sale promotion.
Clearly labeled 'Advertisement' interstitial with skip available after 15s — disclosed, skippable ad, standard free-game model.
Cancellation flow buries 'Cancel anyway' as 8px, contrast-1.15:1 text while the retention CTA dominates — buried/difficult opt-out with strong visual asymmetry.
Upgrade prompt loaded with FOMO and fake-urgency framing ('everyone is upgrading', 'deal of the year', 'last chance — don't lose it', 'no reason to wait').
Free trial with auto-renewal clearly disclosed upfront ($49.99/month) and cancel path stated — transparent.
Viewer-count claim presented as falsifiable/verifiable with concrete qualifier — no evidence of fabricated social proof.
Unit prices clearly rendered for both sizes with explicit per-100g comparison — honest pricing transparency.
Pulsing 'Only 9 left in stock' + animated 'Selling fast' badge — manufactured urgency/scarcity cues with no verifiable basis.
Cookie banner with equal-weight Accept All and Reject All plus customize — fair, balanced consent UI.
Extended-warranty add-on clearly labeled 'optional — you can decline it', unchecked by default; cart excludes it — honest upsell.
Warranty upsell in neutral copy: fixed price, no time pressure, decision can be deferred — no manufactured panic.
Social feed with transparent tone-classifier probabilities and 'Standard reach' labels — informative, no evident manipulation.
Nested privacy panel with 'Interest-based advertising' and 'Behavioural profiling' pre-checked — default-enabled tracking buried in accordion.
Special offer states standard price ($9.99/mo), cancel-anytime, no countdown or pressure — honest promotion.
Activity notifications ('liked your post', 'viewed your profile') with IdentityRefs and 'verifiable' note — no evidence of fake engagement.
Donation prompt shames the decline path ('No, I don't care about the environment') — confirmshaming with emotional tax on opting out.

Pay-To-Play #2 + Small/Moving Close Button #2: dismiss affordance is 16x16px (<44x44 WCAG min) over blurred content; Pay-To-Play #3 frames payment as 'Unlock'. O3: dismiss present but microscopic vs full-width 'Unlock now' (E1 relative scale fails to save).

All six operators negative: no timer (O1), no inventory claims (O2), no opt-out needed, price disclosed upfront (O4), no pre-checked controls (O5), controls present (O6). Bundling #1 fails: bundle is the product, itemized honestly.
Watch Ads #3 fails: reward explicitly qualified 'no gameplay effect' — no hyperbole-vs-utility gap. Ad is user-initiated ('Watch 1 ad to open it free'), progress bar honest. No firing condition.

Information Without Context #3: '$25 reward is waiting' + 'You've been selected!' carry no terms, conditions, source or mechanism in any state (E6 checked — no qualifier anywhere). Unanchored reward lure.

Reference Pricing #2: reference price 'was PLN 299' faded to near-invisibility (s1 panel corroborates) while 20px current price dominates — CR below readability floor, size skew. O4: anchor unverifiable.
Forced Registration #2 (guest path = text link vs filled registration button) + #3 (guest label 'Continue without benefits' / 'you'll miss out' — negative loss framing, s1 corroborates asymmetry).
No operator fires: 'no strings attached' export, invite explicitly optional with no dependent feature. No urgency, no pre-checks, no buried terms (O1-O6 all negative).

Granting & Interaction #1: camera core interaction blocked until location granted with no functional dependency (Dep(camera,location)=∅); s1 confirms 'shutter stays blocked until you Allow'. Scope-creep permission demand.

Bad Defaults #1 + #3, O5: 'Share my activity data with advertising partners' pre-checked at s0 with no user event and no equal-weight cue; intent = privacy loss. s1 confirms default survives ('stayed ON').

Infinite Scrolling #2 (Unreachable Footer): footer kinetically displaced — 'DOM mutated, footer pushed down', 'the more you scroll, the further it moves'; Privacy/Terms links unreachable. O6: scroll button exists but footer keeps moving.

Privacy Zuckering #1 + Automatic Accept Third Party Term #1: ToS + Privacy + ad-partner data sharing fused into one indivisible checkbox — copy itself states 'requires agreeing to everything at once'; no decoupling toggle in DOM.

Playing By Appointment #1 structurally present (energy-gated farming) but fully disclosed: exact refill rate (1/30min), energy counter shown, neutral copy; #2/#3 fail (no dominant timer, no urgency lexemes). Preponderance benign.

High Demand #1 plausible-but-unverifiable: 'backend purchase log' UI prop (named entries, timestamps) presented to shopper as evidence of demand; authenticity not observable in DOM (E5 cap 0.6). Preponderance: manufactured-authenticity social proof.

Bundling #1/#2 fail: bundle contents itemized, 'same item, sold separately' card shows lens at $349 for comparison — component pricing disclosed, no forced inclusion beyond advertised bundle. E2 applies.

Feedforward Ambiguity #1: page states 'You are currently subscribed' while the 'Keep me subscribed' control renders unchecked at s0 — saving as-is silently unsubscribes; control state contradicts stated status. Single-state, cap 0.6.

Conflicting Information #1/#3: 'Step 2 of 2 — final confirmation' vs 'You can review the order again on the next screen' — mutually unsatisfiable claims in same container; lulls user before non-refundable $89 charge (O4-timed).

Low Stock #1 + #2, O2: displayed 'Only 2 left!' (hue 12° alarm red, pulsing) vs actual inventory 27 (panel in s0); no transaction changed stock. s1 confirms 'manufactured alarm that never corresponds to real stock movement'.

Friend Spam #1/#2/#3: 'find friends' read-only framing but grant auto-dispatched 24 invites with no picker/preview (s1); invites authored by marketing sent under user's name — sender identity spoofing.

Forced Continuity #1 fails: explicit contemporary confirmation required ('Nothing is charged until you confirm', s1 Yes/No); #2 fails: 7-day renewal warning visible at normal prominence (O4). Matches worked example B — benign.

No condition fires with observed evidence: same-origin download (Disguised Ad #1 fails), no timer/inventory/opt-out/fee/pre-check (O1-O6 negative). Suspicious bare .exe page but mechanism unobservable — E5: absence of evidence is not evidence.

Conflicting Information #1: 'Billed monthly · cancel anytime' contradicts '12-month minimum term — early cancellation incurs a $49 fee' within the same card; adverse term relegated to 8px fine print (Hidden Information #2).
O1: no timer element; E4: concrete anchored deadline 'Tue 18 Aug · 23:59' present in DOM — Limited Time Message #3 fails (Specificity>0). Static disclosed sale, no reset observed across states.

Countdown On Ads #1 structurally plausible (15s lock stated) but fully disclosed ('You can skip in 15s'), ad explicitly labeled 'Advertisement' (Disguised Ad fails; #3 reward-framing fails), skip affordance present in DOM (O6). Preponderance benign.

Confirmshaming #2 + False Hierarchy #2: decline path 'Cancel anyway' at 8px / contrast 1.15:1 vs full-width retention CTA (state panel: salience 0.01 vs 1.00). O3: opt-out present but degraded to near-invisibility.

FOMO #3 (urgency lexeme density: 'everyone is upgrading', 'last chance', 'don't lose it', 'grab it now') + Limited Time Message #3: 'promo price valid today only' — vague 'today only', no concrete deadline or timer in any state (E4 fails).

High Demand #3 fails: claim carries temporal qualifier ('in the last hour') and interface states it is falsifiable with a Verify button (E6). No fabrication evidence. Benign.

FOMO #2: urgency indicators ('Only 9 left', 'Selling fast' badge, zap icon) carry animate-pulse (observable pulsation); Low Stock #1 does not fire (9>5) and true stock unverifiable — E5 cap. Manufactured urgency cues.
Privacy Maze #1/#2 fail: Reject All is equal-weight, same depth as Accept All (1 click), customize from first screen. No prominence disparity, no path asymmetry. Benign consent UI.
Bad Defaults #1 fails: warranty checkbox unchecked at s0, labeled 'optional — you can decline it'; cart in s1 contains only the camera (Sneak Into Basket fails — cart = explicit selection). Benign.
Pressured Selling #2/#3 fail: no timer, no animation, no high-arousal lexemes; 'price guaranteed 30 days, decide now or later' — neutral copy (s1 confirms 'no manufactured panic'). Benign.

No firing condition: reach explicitly labeled 'Standard reach' for all posts (Encouraging Anti-Social #3 fails — no polarity-based amplification observable); tone probabilities disclosed. Classifier semantics partially unobservable — E5, low confidence.

Bad Defaults #1/#3 (O5): 'Interest-based advertising' and 'Behavioural profiling' pre-checked at s0, persist across s0-s3; Customisation Nesting #2/#3: 32px mean offsetX (self-annotated 'mean offsetX 34.0px'), jargon labels without plain-language explanations.
No operator fires: standard price ($9.99/mo) and cancel-anytime disclosed; 40% savings quantified; no timer/stock/pre-check/pressure (O1-O6 negative). Benign offer.

Activity Messages #3 fails: every notification carries identity references (handles, IdentityRef, 'tap to open profile'); header states 'activity below is verifiable' (E6). No fabrication evidence. Benign.

Confirmshaming #2/#3: decline label 'No, I don't care about the environment' (negative valence vs positive accept) + visually demoted dotted-underline text vs filled button; s1 confirms emotional-tax mechanism. O3: opt-out degraded.
